summary: H.R. 9607, the 'Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act,' moves specific education and workforce development programs, personnel, and funding from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration.

affected_groups.effect: Personnel related to the transferred functions are moved to the Department of Labor.
affected_groups.group: Department of Education employees and personnel

affected_groups.effect: The Department assumes new administrative functions, programs, and personnel from the Department of Education.
affected_groups.group: Department of Labor employees and personnel

key_provisions: Transfers functions of the Office of Career, Technical, and Adult Education from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration.
Moves personnel, assets, contracts, property, records, and unexpended appropriations associated with the transferred functions to the Department of Labor.
Requires the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to ensure the law causes no net increase in full-time equivalent employees at the affected federal agencies.
Requires the OMB Director to certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees on the effective date.
Ensures that pending suits, legal documents, proceedings, and applications for benefits or services are not affected by the transfer.
Sets the general effective date of the Act to six months after enactment, while allowing early implementation of transfers.
missing_information: The exact number of personnel and amount of appropriations being transferred are not specified.
Long-term budgetary savings or costs resulting from the transfer are not provided.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9607, the 'Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act,' moves specific education and workforce development programs, personnel, and funding from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration.
summary_detail.significance: The bill shifts administrative control and oversight of federal adult education, family literacy, and career and technical education programs from the Department of Education to the Department of Labor, aiming to reorganize federal workforce development responsibilities.
